items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline ("shorter than a football pitch", "glued that rock to Africa", "walk it in a minute", "Seriously.", "share custody", "Probably for the best"). Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy: a pompous, triumphant French envoy; an offended little town; then an exhausted, deadpan island.
lines: You think Spain has two neighbours. It has five.
And one border is shorter than a football pitch.
Portugal. France. And tiny Andorra, under a third the size of London.
Britain, through Gibraltar. And Morocco... in Africa.
Say-oo-ta, Meh-lee-ya, and a Spanish rock right off the coast.
In nineteen thirty-four, a storm piled up sand and glued that rock to Africa.
New border: about eighty-five metres. You could walk it in a minute.
But Spain's weirdest borders aren't in Africa. They're with France. So how?
Rewind to sixteen fifty-nine. Spain and France sign peace on a tiny river island.
Spain hands France thirty-three villages in the mountains.
[pompous, triumphant] Thirty-three villages! Yee-vee-ah, you're French now!
[offended, indignant] Excuse me? I'm a town.
Seriously. So Yee-vee-ah stayed Spanish, surrounded by France on every side.
Its road to Spain still runs through France. About one point six kilometres of it.
And that's still not the strangest part.
Remember that river island? Neither country would let it go.
So they share custody. February to July, it's Spanish.
August to January, French. They've swapped like this for over a hundred and twenty years.
Nobody lives there. Honestly? Probably for the best.
[exhausted, deadpan] Am I Spanish or French? Check the calendar.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
